subject: Calibration: cross-team variance triage & HR-privileged case handling
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Calibration: cross-team variance triage & HR-privileged case handling

Team —

After yesterday's calibration run I pulled a cross-team summary (attached) and flagged two things that need immediate triage ahead of manager sign-off:

1) A ~12-point shift between Team A and Team B on the "consistency" axis (many more low ratings in Team A than expected).
2) One sensitive manager-level case where comments suggest possible bias/retaliation and we should treat the details as HR-privileged.

Please review the attached rating_spread_Q1-2027.csv and tell me: (a) whether you agree with the proposed anchors for slotting, and (b) for the sensitive case, whether we should perform an HR-privileged handoff now or treat it as a normal calibration exception.

I'm proposing a short breakout at 2pm PT today (30m) if we can all make it. If not, we'll run a quick async path with the template Rishi recommended.

Thanks —
Jordan
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rating_spread_Q1-2027.csv (csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Calibration: cross-team variance triage & HR-privileged case handling

On Thu, Mar 4, 2027 at 9:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> After yesterday's calibration run I pulled a cross-team summary (attached) and flagged two things that need immediate triage ahead of manager sign-off:
> 
> 1) A ~12-point shift between Team A and Team B on the "consistency" axis (many more low ratings in Team A than expected).
> 2) One sensitive manager-level case where comments suggest possible bias/retaliation and we should treat the details as HR-privileged.
> 
> Please review the attached rating_spread_Q1-2027.csv and tell me: (a) whether you agree with the proposed anchors for slotting, and (b) for the sensitive case, whether we should perform an HR-privileged handoff now or treat it as a normal calibration exception.

Jordan — quick read through. My immediate thoughts:

- Anchors: I agree with three anchor points you proposed (Top, Meets, Needs). Team A's mode is shifted low relative to historical cohort; I think it's partly manager-stringency but also a comp of recent reorg hires. Suggested action: apply a +1 anchor lift on consistency for the midband of Team A and re-evaluate promotion/bonus cutoffs.

- Sensitive case: this looks like Manager M-17. The comments include phrasing that suggests candidate raised a concern about the manager; that crosses into possible retaliation territory. I think we should stop all non-essential distribution of case details and move to an HR-privileged handoff.

I attached a redacted summary for the group (sensitive-case-summary-redacted.pdf) — redacts names and direct allegations but preserves timelines and rating spread.

If we go HR-privileged, we should: 1) limit the distribution list to the people who need to know, 2) use the privileged-handoff-template to transmit to HR/legal, and 3) defer final sign-off on that person until HR confirms next steps.

Happy to join the 2pm breakout; I think we should block it for 45 minutes in case we need to go deeper.

— Laura
Director, People Ops (comp & performance partner)

Attachments: sensitive-case-summary-redacted.pdf (pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 10:18:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Calibration: cross-team variance triage & HR-privileged case handling

Jordan / Laura —

Thanks for the notes. I'm aligned with Laura on the +1 anchor lift for Team A midband as a conservative step; we should capture the rationale in the calibration notes (I can draft).

On the sensitive manager case — agree we need HR-privileged handling. Two operational asks:

1) Can Rishi draft the privileged-handoff (templated) and include an itemized evidence list so HR can triage quickly?
2) I'll schedule the breakout for 2:00 — put a short pre-read in the Drive link and mark the meeting as SENSITIVE (internal leadership only).

If Laura can confirm who must remain on the list (I suggest Jordan, Laura, Vivek, Rishi, and HR lead), I'll remove non-essential folks from the thread.

— Vivek
Head of Product Ops

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:02:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Calibration: cross-team variance triage & HR-privileged case handling

Jordan / team —

I've drafted a privileged handoff note and an evidence checklist (privileged-handoff-template.docx). Key items included: timeline of events, anonymized witness list, copies of the manager's feedback thread (redacted), and the compressed rating distribution for the person in question.

Operational suggestions:
- Use encrypted delivery to HR/legal (DocuSign or secure upload) — do not reply-all with the document.
- Document any interim actions (e.g., temporary reporting change) as "pending HR review" in the calibration minutes.
- If HR requests an interview, the manager should be notified only after HR has a plan.

I'll attach the template to the breakout calendar item and can be the point for consolidation.

— Rishi
Sr. People Ops Partner

Attachments: privileged-handoff-template.docx (docx)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Adele Thornton <adele@peopleops.co>, Tom Saunders <tom.s@acmegames.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 12:35:07 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Calibration: cross-team variance triage & HR-privileged case handling

Adele / Tom — forwarding for visibility.

Adele — we have a case that Laura flagged as potentially involving retaliation. We've redacted the summary and attached a privilege-hand off draft (internal). Can you review our proposed privileged handoff approach and confirm any additional evidence HR outside counsel will request? We want to be sure we don't accidentally expand the distribution and preserve privilege.

Tom — FYI for Acme Games (your POC for the integration team) — note that we are pausing any final manager-level action for the impacted individual. We'll update you after HR has a path.

Jordan
VP, Engineering

Attachments forwarded: sensitive-case-summary-redacted.pdf (pdf)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Calibration: cross-team variance triage & HR-privileged case handling

Thanks — I've received the redacted summary and the draft handoff.

Next steps from HR side (timeline):
1) I will intake the privileged bundle by EOD today via secure upload.
2) HR/legal will run a preliminary conflict analysis by tomorrow noon.
3) We will not inform the manager until HR has completed initial interviews and confirmed whether protective measures are needed.

Please keep the distribution tight to the five of us for now. I'll post a brief status update to the Drive link once intake is complete. If any of you receive questions from other leaders, please refer them to me.

— Neha Kapoor
Head of HR Operations

Note: privileged-handoff-template.docx attached to the secure intake (not on thread).
